claims.text: Introducing nano-coupled grains and embedded nanoprecipitates into CoCrFeNi will provide adaptive friction-interface protection from room temperature to 800 °C.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has a relatively homogeneous microstructure.
CoCrFeNi suffers elevated friction and wear at high temperatures because of rapid softening and inadequate tribo-oxidative protection.
A thermal treatment or minor compositional modification can induce controlled nano-coupled grains and homogeneously dispersed nanoprecipitates in CoCrFeNi.
The relevant structural mediator is the formation of nano-coupled grains and well-dispersed nanoprecipitates.
At low temperatures, the nanohierarchical structure enables multiple deformation pathways that distribute frictional stress in stages.
Distributing frictional stress through multiple deformation pathways reduces localized wear at low temperatures.
At high temperatures, the heterostructure promotes formation of a dense nanocrystalline tribo-oxide glaze layer.
The nanocrystalline glaze layer acts as a lubricious barrier that limits adhesive and oxidative wear.
The engineered CoCrFeNi alloy will have a lower coefficient of friction than standard CoCrFeNi throughout the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The engineered CoCrFeNi alloy will have lower wear rates than standard CoCrFeNi throughout the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The engineered alloy may attain wear rates on the order of 10^-7 to 10^-6 mm^3/Nm.
The proposed operating boundary is approximately 25–800 °C under a normal load around 5 N in linear reciprocating sliding.
The operating environment should not promote oxidation beyond that typical of standard tribological tests.
Prior evidence demonstrates adaptive nanohierarchical heterostructures in a different multicomponent alloy system.
The processing conditions required to create the proposed nanoscale structure in CoCrFeNi are not yet established.
The long-term stability of the protective glaze under cyclic thermal and mechanical stresses is undetermined.
